name: Wealthfront Engineering Blog
description: Engineering blog covering fintech infrastructure, mobile development, database engineering, and software architecture at Wealthfront.

posts.title: Putting the Tech in Fintech: How We Use FIX to Execute Trades at Scale
posts.author: Grace Sun
posts.summary: Wealthfront explains how they leverage the FIX (Financial Information eXchange) protocol to execute thousands of trades efficiently, covering their four-layer infrastructure: networking, protocol, QuickFIX/J library, and an internal application layer that translates between domain objects and FIX messages.

posts.title: How we standardized MariaDB in our Integration Server
posts.author: Eloy Gonzalez
posts.summary: Wealthfront migrated their Integration Server from HSQLDB to MariaDB to achieve better test/production parity, using Testcontainers to manage MariaDB instances in Docker and socket mounting for CI/CD pipeline compatibility.

posts.title: XcodeGen and the quest to modularize the Wealthfront iOS app
posts.author: Matthew Bommer
posts.summary: Wealthfront's iOS engineering team adopted XcodeGen to eliminate merge conflicts on binary project files and enable modularization of their 10-year-old monolithic app into independently compilable Swift packages with enforced architectural boundaries.

posts.title: New Leaders, New Perspectives: Why We Joined Wealthfront Engineering
posts.author: Wealthfront Engineering
posts.summary: New engineering leaders share their perspectives on joining Wealthfront and what drew them to the company's engineering culture and mission.

posts.title: The Hidden Cost of Convenience: Rethinking Old ORM Patterns for Scale
posts.author: Andrew Houts
posts.summary: Wealthfront rewrote their portfolio balance calculation system to address severe performance degradation caused by inefficient Hibernate ORM patterns, achieving approximately a tenth of the original processing time by adopting dependency injection and proper separation of concerns.

posts.title: Automating Exhaustive Branch Coverage for Sealed Types in Kotlin
posts.author: Sean Amos
posts.summary: Wealthfront created a custom JUnit Test Runner using @Exhaustive and @ExhaustiveCase annotations to automatically enforce that all subtypes of Kotlin sealed classes have corresponding unit tests, eliminating manual code review checks for test completeness.
